title: Automotive Vulnerability Disclosure: Stakeholders, Opportunities, Challenges

original_source.central_claim: automotive-specific coordinated disclosure with flexible negotiated grace periods, clear stakeholder roles and trusted information sharing

central_claims: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure adapted to automotive safety, supplier complexity and long lifetimes is preferable to uncoordinated disclosure.
Automotive patching and grace periods should be case-specific, transparent and negotiated rather than copied as rigid IT deadlines.
Clear stakeholder responsibilities, trusted coordination and information sharing can improve automotive vulnerability management.

source_manifest.title: Automotive Vulnerability Disclosure: Stakeholders, Opportunities, Challenges
source_manifest.finding: Reviews automotive disclosure and proposes tailored coordination, stakeholder responsibilities and flexible patching periods; a quantitative grace-period metric is future work.

source_manifest.title: Reasonable disclosure grace periods for security vulnerabilities in vehicle software — Grace Period Calculator
source_manifest.finding: Official project page presents a developed calculator implementing vulnerability-specific time/process criteria and links the target among its foundational publications; external deployment is not documented.

source_manifest.title: Your Disclosure Is Important To Us: An Analysis of Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Responses Using a Real Security Issue
source_manifest.finding: Independent empirical disclosure campaign cites the target as automotive background; studies email vulnerabilities and finds many unresolved reports despite policies.

source_manifest.title: Survey on Vulnerability Report Handling in the Automotive Environment
source_manifest.finding: Kaya and Bolz assess OEM and supplier reporting options and note insufficient transparency/data; Bolz is an original author.

source_manifest.title: Managing the Inevitable – A Maturity Model to Establish Incident Response Management Capabilities
source_manifest.finding: Develops an incident-response maturity model and lists the target among references; accessible text did not establish how that specific reference affected its construction.

answers.rationale: No later independent study directly tests whether the full automotive-specific coordination and flexible-deadline proposal improves outcomes; the email campaign studies another setting.
This is primarily a normative review. No independent reconstruction and evaluation of its specific automotive process proposal was verified.
The later OEM survey shares an author and acknowledges limited data; the independent email study is not a stronger automotive test.
Later papers recognize the review as relevant literature but do not explicitly retain or reject its complete recommendation set.
The grace-period calculator addresses a gap identified in the review, but building that metric does not establish that the original proposal survived an empirical limitations test.
The calculator and OEM survey overlap authors. The independent campaign cites the review as background; no qualifying independent extension was established.
Independent citations exist, but no two teams were verified to substantively build on the specific process proposal.
The email campaign uses established disclosure standards rather than this automotive adaptation; maturity-model citation context was insufficient to establish actual reuse.
No later review explicitly identifies this contribution as enabling a new research direction; automotive disclosure predates it.
No independent head-to-head evaluation of the proposed adapted process against fixed-deadline or other disclosure regimes was verified.
The calculator’s promised prioritization benefit is stated by its developers; an independent measured benefit remains unverified.
The independent email experiment is related research, not an application of this automotive process outside its original setting.

The authors developed the proposed next-step capability: a calculator that quantifies vulnerability-specific grace periods. This is documented technical development, without claiming independent validation or industrial deployment.

evidence.explanation: The original explicitly identifies a future grace-period metric.
The official successor project implements that specific capability and links the target research.

answers.rationale: The official page offers a calculator and possible use cases, but does not document an OEM, coordinator or standard actually adopting it.
No fair independent comparison verifies the claimed advantage of tailored periods over fixed deadlines in automotive remediation.
An active project page exists and later citations occur, but substantive use of the original framework after May 2024 is not established by deployment or a dated implementation report.
The 2026 empirical paper cites the target as background without an explicit positive assessment of its central recommendations.
The 2022 survey shares an author; later independent references lack verified substantive reuse, so two independent follow-up years are unresolved.
An independent maturity-model article includes the target in its bibliography, but its specific synthesis role could not be verified from accessible text.
The developer maintains related documentation; this does not establish continued effectiveness despite competing standards or processes.

search_gaps: Full original PDF read from a scholarly mirror after publisher access failures.
Independent maturity-model full text was not retrieved; the thesis mirror lists the publication without its full article. Its citation is not upgraded to use.
The calculator page is undated; its date is an explicit as-of observation, not an invented publication date.
No exhaustive audit of proprietary OEM security workflows was possible.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; the assigned pilot sample is not an unbiased estimate of all research outcomes.
research.summary: The proposal led into the original team’s documented grace-period calculator. Independent effectiveness, reproduction and operational adoption were not established by the sources read; citations and existing disclosure standards are not treated as proof of uptake.
